name: Receiving Input Integers Until a Certain Condition is Met (Case 4)
description: Construct a program that receives an integer from the user, outputs that integer, and stops receiving integers when the user enters an even integer less than 10.
code:
#Step 1: Read the first integer that the user enters
text = input("Enter an integer:")
num = int(text)
#Step 2: Print the integer that the user has entered, then receive the next integers as long as the user enters an integer that is not even or is not less than 10; otherwise stop
while num % 2 != 0 or num >= 10 :
    print("The integer entered is:", num)
    text = input("Enter an integer:")
    num = int(text)
print("End of input.")

1.content: #Step 1: Read the first integer that the user enters

commentList: We need to read and process the input value that the user enters. To read the input value from the user, we need to use the input() function. This statement prompts the user to enter the integer, then reads the text entered by the user and places it in the variable text. The value that will be stored in variable text is a string.
We need to convert the input text to its integer representation. For this purpose, we use the conversion function int().

Note that the conversion to integer can only be done if the string actually presents a number. If the input number is a float, the int() function cuts off the fractional part of the floating-point number to create an integer.

4.content: #Step 2: Print the integer that the user has entered, then receive the next integers as long as the user enters an integer that is not even or is not less than 10; otherwise stop

commentList:
We need to repeat receiving the integers from the user as long as the user enters an integer that is not even or is not less than 10. Therefore, we need to use a loop structure. Since we don't know ahead of time how many times the loop will be repeated, we need to use a while loop. The condition in the while loop tests whether the body of the loop should be repeated, so it should test whether the input integer is not even or not less than 10.

We check whether the input integer is not even by checking whether the remainder when the integer is divided by 2 is not zero. We could check whether the input integer is not less than 10 by checking whether the input integer is greater than or equal to 10.

The body of the while loop is repeated as long as the user enters an integer that is not even or is not less than 10. The loop terminates when the loop condition evaluates to False, that is when the user enters an even integer less than 10.
Note that the or operator yields the result True if at least one of the conditions is True. Also note that the % operator returns the remainder of the division.

This statement prints to the default standard output stream the text "The integer entered is:" and the value of variable num.
The printed text shows the arguments of the print function separated by the default delimiter (i.e., single space character) and followed by the end-of-line character at the end.

We need to read and process the next input value that the user enters. To read the input value from the user, we need to use the input() function. This statement prompts the user to enter the integer, then reads the text entered by the user and places it in the variable text. The value that will be stored in variable text is a string.
We need to convert the input text to its integer representation. For this purpose, we use the conversion function int().

Note that the conversion to integer can only be done if the string actually presents a number. If the input number is a float, the int() function cuts off the fractional part of the floating-point number to create an integer.
We inform the user that this is the end of input. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
